You have to change the pronoun if you are reporting what someone else said. Compare these two sentences. In each case the person actually said "I don't want to go."

• I said, “I don't want to go.” > I said I didn't want to go.
  • Bill said, “I don't want to go.” > Bill said he didn't want to go.

You use could have, should have and would have to talk about things that were possible in the past and may or may not have happened.

The structure:

Subject + modal verb + have + verb (past participle)
I could have done
You should have made
She would have said

You use could have to talk about possibilities if something had been different in the past.
For example: I could have made sure that I finished on time.

You use should have to talk about past events that did not happen and to speculate about events that may or may not have happened.
For example: I should have confirmed that it had to be in before 5:00 p.m.

You use should not have to speculate negatively about what may or may not have happened.
You also use should not have to express regret for past actions.

You use would have to imagine a result if something had been different in the past.
For example: It would have been on time if I had been clear on the deadline.
* Would have expresses more certainty about the result than could have.
I should have confirmed that it had to be in before 5:00 p.m. but I didn't.
If I had confirmed the deadline, I would have known it had to be finished at 5:00 p.m.
I could have made sure that I finished on time.
It would have been on time if I had been clear on the deadline.

images.text: You know the expression “It's not my day”? Well, it's not my week. Things really aren't going my way. Maybe I'm just overly sensitive, but I'm very frustrated right now. Here's why. I had a blog assignment due last Friday. My boss told me I had to hand in the piece by the end of the day on Friday. I was really busy that day and was stressed out.

I should have confirmed that it had to be in before 5:00 p.m. but I didn't. I told her I would submit it by the end of the day. Unfortunately, there was a misunderstanding. I thought the end of day was at midnight and my boss thought it was at 5:00 p.m., the end of the work day. If I had confirmed the deadline, I would have known it had to be finished at 5:00 p.m. I could have made sure that I finished on time.

Instead, I worked on other things and I finished my piece at home after dinner. I sent it to my boss at 11:30 p.m. This morning she asked if I could come to her office.  She seemed really angry! She said that my assignment was late and that she was disappointed with me. I told her I was very sorry and that it would have been on time if I had been clear on the deadline.
